Caroline — thanks for the clear list, and the spreadsheet is helpful.

Quick answers up-front, and a proposed playbook below so procurement/legal have a concrete starting point:

- SOC 2: Redwood completed a Type II audit covering Jan–Dec 2025; the latest report (June 2026 bridge summary + full report) is available to customers under NDA. We propose confirming availability in the exhibit: "Customer may request the latest SOC 2 Type II report and related bridge letters; Redwood will provide subject to NDA and reasonable redaction for third-party data."

- Pen test: proposed default is "annual" with a 45-day advance notice to Redwood and an agreement to run tests against a staging environment unless otherwise agreed. For customers that require production testing, we propose a separate scoped exception with a higher-level sign-off (and a mutually agreed runbook).

- Evidence cadence: recommend a quarterly artifact bundle (SOC/controls evidence snapshot) plus an on-demand ticket for ad-hoc evidence requests. We can provide a calendar (.ics) with two-week evidence windows each quarter to make procurement audits predictable.

- Audit rights carve-outs: propose limiting broad "forensic access" language and instead offering scoped inspection rights tied to SOC 2 assertions and bounded pen-test activities. We suggest specific carve-outs: subpoena/forensic access only with legal process; no live exfiltration tests; subcontractor evidence via certified reports.

Attached: a first-pass redline for the security exhibit (Redwood_Brightwell_security-exhibit_redline_v1.pdf) and an example evidence calendar (evidence_window_calendar.ics).

If that approach looks good, next step is: 1) legal redline, 2) procurement confirms calendar dates, 3) security teams align on pen-test scope.

I can take point on the technical details during the legal review — looping Karthik and Laura for operational and legal voice. Happy to set a 30-min sync tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,

Marissa / Karthik — legal redline guidance below. High-level we should be cooperative but limit legal exposure: 

1) Audit rights: carve back to "inspection limited to SOC 2 and specifically enumerated controls" and require a written scope and 30-day notice for any inspection beyond SOC 2. Absolutely carve out forensic access unless compelled by legal process.
2) Data retention / redaction: include explicit statements that Redwood will redact third-party and personal data from any shared artifacts where feasible.
3) Pen test: accept "annual" with a defined advance notice window — I prefer 60 days, but 45 is defensible if Karthik confirms ops can meet that. Also require both parties to sign a scoped test plan prior to testing.
4) Remedies & discovery: limit discovery to technical artifacts directly tied to the tested controls; no open-ended data dumps.

I'll attach a short note with inline redline language for the security exhibit. We should route the redline back to Brightwell with a comment summary and a HubSpot note.
